implementation_notes: The compiler already does escape analysis and inlining; fight it with `-gcflags=-m` before hand-optimising. Use pprof (CPU and heap profiles) as the standard instrument. For hot paths, avoid interface dispatch in inner loops and prefer slices over maps.
idiom_name: pprof CPU/heap profiles + -gcflags escape analysis output
pitfalls: Building with -race in a benchmark (it distorts timings)
Optimising map lookups before checking whether the profile shows them
Allocation churn hidden behind a fast-looking microbenchmark
